verdict.label: BUY — First SPX Close Above 7,460; NVDA Day 2 Confirmed; Tuesday Armed
verdict.rationale_short: The S&P 500 closed at 7,473.47 — the first definitive session close above the 7,460 BUY trigger this series has tracked — completing the primary regime condition. NVDA closed at $218.13, confirming Day 2 of the post-earnings consolidation and arming the Tuesday May 26 execution entry at $216–220. VIX declined to 16.76 and the 30Y eased to 5.064%, both directionally healing but not yet through their respective BUY thresholds. Conviction stays medium: the 30Y two-session confirmation clock has not started, the 72-hour Memorial Day gap leaves Iran/oil risk unquantified, and the IWM short thesis faces its second consecutive contradicting session. Execute NVDA $216–220 Tuesday open; size broad BUY at 50–60% pending May 28 PCE outcome.

bear_case: The S&P 500 has posted eight consecutive weekly gains — a streak that historically precedes consolidation or reversion, not sustained acceleration. VIX at 16.76 and Fear & Greed at 61 confirm sentiment is in greed territory, not the capitulation-reset zone that historically produces high-conviction BUY entries; the marginal buyer pool thins with each additional gain week. The 30Y at 5.064% has not yet started the two-session close below 5.05%, and a 72-hour Memorial Day gap with WTI at $98 and no formal Iran resolution means Tuesday could open with an adverse geopolitical shock. May 28 PCE at >2.5% YoY would immediately confirm the 30Y structural floor, push yields back toward 5.15–5.20%, and require abandoning the BUY call before it is fully sized. If SPX closes below 7,400 with the 30Y above 5.15% on any session through May 28, Step Aside is activated and the NVDA execution entry is abandoned.
